title: The function Artin–Schreier cover, its root, constants and induced fibre map
statement: For a scheme $X$, a natural number $n$, and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, let $A_n:\mathbf A^1_X\to\mathbf A^1_X$ be $t\mapsto t^n-t$, and let $s_f:X\to\mathbf A^1_X$ be the section with coordinate $f$, using affine space [def-sbc-affine-space]. Define the function cover $Y_{n,f}=\mathbf A^1_X\times_{A_n,\mathbf A^1_X,s_f}X$ by the chosen fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], its projection $\pi_{n,f}:Y_{n,f}\to X$ to be the second projection, and its tautological root $y_{n,f}\in\Gamma(Y_{n,f},\mathcal O_{Y_{n,f}})$ to be the pullback of the coordinate along the first projection. When $X$ is a scheme over a field $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], its base-constant map $k\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is the inverse of the canonical global-sections identification for $\operatorname{Spec}k$, followed by pullback along the given structure morphism. For schemes $Y,Z,T$, morphisms $\pi:Y\to X$, $\rho:Z\to X$, $x:T\to X$ and $a:Y\to Z$ satisfying $\rho\circ a=\pi$, define the induced fibre map $Y\times_XT\to Z\times_XT$ to be the functorial pullback map determined by $a$ and $\operatorname{id}_T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. In characteristic $p$ the specialization $n=p$ is the auxiliary cover $y^p-y=f$; this definition itself assumes neither primality nor etaleness.
